meta.title: Sample license waste report - synthetic demo tenant
meta.description: A walkthrough of a LicenseMeter license waste report, computed from the synthetic 155-user demo tenant: per-rule findings with euro figures, the weekly digest, the monthly PDF report and the PowerShell remediation. Not a customer story.

sampleReport.h1: What a license waste report looks like
sampleReport.badge: Synthetic demo tenant - explore it yourself, no account needed
sampleReport.intro: This is not a customer story. “{orgName}” is a fictional fixture tenant of {users} users, deliberately seeded with all six waste patterns so you can see a full report before connecting anything. Every euro figure below is computed from that fixture by the same rules engine that scans real tenants, and the demo workspace showing these exact numbers is one click away.
sampleReport.statsNote: Synthetic figures from the demo fixture, recomputed by the test suite so this page cannot drift from what the live demo shows.
sampleReport.tenantText: A mid-sized organization as the rules engine sees one: a mix of E3, Business Premium, Copilot and connected-app seats, a directory with the usual history of joiners, movers and leavers, and admin consoles that were tidied less often than the org chart changed.
sampleReport.firstScanText: One read-only sync joins directory status, license assignments, sign-in activity and per-workload usage, then the rules engine prices what it finds: {findings} findings worth <waste>€ {amount}</waste> a month, about <waste>€ {annual}</waste> a year.

leavers.flags: Accounts disabled in Entra ID that still hold Microsoft 365 or connected-app seats: the classic offboarding leak.

idle.flags: Licensed people with no sign-in and no Exchange, OneDrive, SharePoint or Teams activity inside the window, or none ever.

shelfware.flags: Purchased seats no one is assigned to: prepaid units minus consumed units, per SKU (shelfware).

copilotUnused.flags: Copilot licenses with no Copilot activity in 60 days.

orphaned.category: App seats with no directory account
orphaned.flags: Connected-app seats whose owner has no Entra ID account at all - orphans left behind by manual admin-console work.

sampleReport.offboardingNote: The offboarding line is the one worth reading twice: {leaverCount} disabled accounts still hold licenses, and {crossVendorLeaverCount} of them also kept Adobe, Zoom, Atlassian, Salesforce or AI seats - waste no single admin console shows, because each one only sees its own slice. Every finding names the account, the rule, the evidence and the monthly cost from the editable price book.

digest.heading: The weekly digest
digest.text: Workspace owners and admins get a short email with the current waste number, what changed in the last seven days and the largest open findings. Waste that appears between visits - a leaver kept a seat, a license went idle - stops depending on someone remembering to check.

pdf.heading: The monthly PDF report
pdf.text: Once a month a board-ready PDF lands in the same inboxes: the recoverable total, every open finding priced, and the trend since last month. For this tenant that is the <waste>€ {amount}</waste> figure, ready to forward to whoever owns the renewal.

script.heading: A script your IT reviews and runs
script.text: For the seats you decide to reclaim, LicenseMeter generates the PowerShell remediation script - the same Graph cmdlets your team would write by hand, scoped to exactly the chosen findings. Your IT reads it, edits it if they like, and runs it themselves. LicenseMeter holds no write permission and never changes the tenant.

acknowledge.heading: Acknowledge what stays
acknowledge.text: Not every flagged seat is waste - the CFO’s barely used license stays. Acknowledging a finding records that decision, and because findings persist across nightly syncs, it stays recorded. If the situation changes, the finding reopens instead of resurfacing as new. Finance gets the CSV of whatever remains open, priced per month.

cta.heading: Open the demo workspace, then get your own number.
cta.text: The sample tenant behind this page is browsable without an account: every finding, the price book, the exports. When you have seen enough, a free read-only scan replaces the synthetic figures with yours - the <security>security overview</security> lists every permission up front.

sampleReport.footerNote: All figures on this page describe the synthetic demo workspace, not a customer environment. LicenseMeter is free, including continuous monitoring. No credit card required.
